name: Barbell back squat
setup: Set the bar in the rack at mid-chest height.
Bar sits on your upper back, below the bony bump of your neck. Feet shoulder-width, toes turned out slightly.
execution: Break at hips and knees together and sit down between your heels.
Go as deep as you can while your back stays neutral.
Drive up through the whole foot, chest and hips rising at the same speed.
breathing: Big breath into your belly and brace before each rep; breathe out near the top.
mistakes: Knees caving in on the way up.
Hips shooting up first, turning it into a good morning.
safety: Set the safety pins just below your bottom position, every time.

name: Barbell front squat
setup: Bar rests on the front of your shoulders, close to your throat.
Elbows high, fingertips under the bar; the grip can be loose.
execution: Sit straight down, keeping your torso tall.
Push your knees forward and out over your toes.
Stand up leading with your elbows.
breathing: Brace hard before you descend; exhale through the top.
mistakes: Elbows dropping, so the bar rolls forward.
safety: If the bar rolls forward, push it away and step back. Use the safety pins.

name: Goblet squat
setup: Hold one dumbbell or kettlebell against your chest with both hands.
Feet a little wider than your hips.
execution: Sit down between your heels, elbows travelling inside your knees.
Pause briefly at the bottom, then stand tall.
breathing: Breathe in on the way down, out as you stand.
mistakes: Letting the weight drift away from your chest.
safety: A great way to learn the squat before loading a barbell.

name: Leg press
setup: Back and hips flat against the pad.
Feet shoulder-width in the middle of the platform.
execution: Release the safeties and lower until your knees reach about 90 degrees.
Press back up without locking your knees hard.
breathing: In on the way down, out as you press.
mistakes: Lowering so far that your hips peel off the seat.
Snapping the knees straight at the top.
safety: Keep your lower back on the pad. If it lifts, shorten the range.

name: Hack squat
setup: Shoulders under the pads, back flat on the backrest.
Feet shoulder-width, slightly forward on the plate.
execution: Release the handles and lower under control.
Drive back up through your mid-foot.
breathing: Brace before each rep; breathe out near the top.
safety: Re-engage the safety handles before stepping out.

name: Smith machine squat
setup: Bar across your upper back, feet slightly in front of the bar.
Set the stops just below your lowest point.
execution: Unhook the bar and sit down until your thighs are about parallel.
Stand up, keeping your back against the bar path.
breathing: Brace before descending; exhale near the top.
mistakes: Feet directly under the bar, which pushes the knees far forward.
safety: Always set the stops. Twist the bar to hook it at the end of the set.

name: Bodyweight squat
setup: Feet shoulder-width, arms out in front for balance.
execution: Sit down as low as you comfortably can with your heels down.
Stand up and squeeze your glutes at the top.
breathing: In on the way down, out on the way up.
safety: Slow the lowering phase to make it harder without load.

name: Barbell deadlift
setup: Bar over your mid-foot, feet hip-width.
Grip just outside your legs, shins touch the bar, back flat.
execution: Pull the slack out of the bar, then push the floor away.
Bar stays close to your legs the whole way.
Finish standing tall with hips through, then lower the same path.
breathing: Brace before every rep; reset your breath at the bottom.
mistakes: Rounding the lower back off the floor.
Bar drifting forward from the legs.
safety: Stop the set when your back can't stay neutral. Form breaks first, injuries follow.

name: Romanian deadlift
setup: Start standing, weight in front of your thighs, knees soft.
execution: Push your hips back while the weight slides down your thighs.
Stop when your hamstrings are fully stretched, usually mid-shin.
Drive your hips forward to stand.
breathing: Breathe in as you hinge; out as you stand.
mistakes: Bending the knees into a squat.
Rounding the back to reach lower.
safety: Range ends where your back stays flat, not where the weight hits the floor.

name: Trap bar deadlift
setup: Stand in the centre of the bar, feet hip-width.
Grip the handles, hips lower than in a straight-bar deadlift.
execution: Push the floor away and stand up tall.
Lower under control along the same path.
mistakes: Standing off-centre, so the bar tilts.
safety: Friendlier on the lower back than a straight bar; a good first deadlift.

name: Hip thrust
setup: Upper back against the bench edge, bar padded across your hips.
Feet flat, about hip-width, shins vertical at the top.
execution: Drive through your heels and lift your hips until your body is flat.
Pause and squeeze your glutes, then lower.
mistakes: Arching the lower back instead of extending the hips.
Feet too far away, so hamstrings take over.
safety: Use a bar pad: the load sits directly on your hip bones.

name: Kettlebell swing
setup: Kettlebell a foot in front of you, feet a bit wider than hips.
execution: Hike the bell back between your legs like a football snap.
Snap your hips forward so the bell floats to chest height.
Let it fall back and hinge to meet it.
breathing: Sharp exhale as your hips snap forward.
safety: The power comes from the hips. Your arms are just ropes.

name: Glute bridge
setup: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat near your glutes.
execution: Press through your heels and lift your hips.
Hold for a second at the top, then lower slowly.
mistakes: Arching the lower back at the top.
safety: Gentle on the back; a good option when hinges are off the table.

name: Single-leg Romanian deadlift
setup: Stand on one leg, slight bend in the knee, weight in the opposite hand.
execution: Hinge forward as the free leg reaches back, hips square to the floor.
Return to standing by driving the hip forward.
breathing: In as you hinge, out as you stand.
safety: Touch a wall or rack with your free hand if balance limits you.

name: Walking lunge
setup: Stand tall, dumbbells at your sides if using them.
execution: Take a long step and lower until your back knee nearly touches the floor.
Push through the front heel and step through into the next lunge.
breathing: In as you lower, out as you rise.
mistakes: Steps too short, so the front knee shoots forward.
safety: Clear the walkway first.

name: Bulgarian split squat
setup: Rear foot laces-down on a bench, front foot about two feet ahead.
execution: Lower straight down until the front thigh is near parallel.
Drive up through the front heel.
breathing: In on the way down, out on the way up.
mistakes: Front foot too close to the bench.
safety: Find your foot position with bodyweight before adding load.

name: Step-up
setup: Face a sturdy box or bench about knee height.
execution: Place one whole foot on the box and drive up through that heel.
Lower slowly with control; switch legs after the set.
mistakes: Box too high, so the hips tip.
safety: Make sure the box can't slide.

name: Reverse lunge
setup: Stand tall, feet hip-width.
execution: Step one foot back and lower until both knees are bent about 90 degrees.
Push through the front heel to return.
breathing: In as you step back, out as you return.
safety: Kinder to the knees than forward lunges.

name: Leg extension
setup: Line your knee up with the machine's pivot, pad on your lower shin.
execution: Straighten your legs fully and pause.
Lower slowly over two to three seconds.
safety: Use moderate loads and controlled reps if your knees are sensitive.

name: Lying leg curl
setup: Lie face down, knees just off the pad, roller above your heels.
execution: Curl your heels toward your glutes.
Lower slowly to almost straight.
safety: Keep hips pressed down to protect the lower back.

name: Standing calf raise
setup: Balls of your feet on a step or platform, heels hanging off.
execution: Rise as high as you can and pause.
Lower slowly into a deep stretch.
safety: Pause in the stretch; calves respond to full range.

name: Barbell bench press
setup: Eyes under the bar, feet flat, shoulder blades squeezed together.
Grip so forearms are vertical at the bottom.
execution: Lower the bar to your lower chest with elbows about 45 degrees from your body.
Press up and slightly back toward your face.
breathing: Breath and brace before lowering; exhale after the hardest part.
mistakes: Bouncing the bar off the chest.
safety: Use safety arms or a spotter for heavy sets. Never use a thumbless grip.

name: Incline barbell press
setup: Bench at about 30 degrees, shoulder blades pinched.
execution: Lower the bar to your upper chest.
Press straight up over your shoulders.
breathing: Brace before lowering; exhale near the top.
mistakes: Bench too steep, so it becomes a shoulder press.
safety: Use safety arms set just below chest height.

name: Dumbbell bench press
setup: Sit with the dumbbells on your thighs, then kick them up as you lie back.
execution: Lower until the dumbbells are beside your chest.
Press up and slightly together.
breathing: In on the way down, out as you press.
mistakes: Letting the dumbbells drift toward your face.
Dropping them out wide at the end.
safety: Bring the dumbbells back to your thighs as you sit up; don't drop them beside you.

name: Incline dumbbell press
setup: Bench at 30 to 45 degrees, dumbbells kicked up from your thighs.
execution: Lower to the sides of your upper chest.
Press up over your shoulders.
breathing: In on the way down, out as you press.
safety: A shoulder-friendly alternative to the barbell incline.

name: Push-up
setup: Hands a bit wider than shoulders, body in one straight line.
execution: Lower until your chest is a fist above the floor.
Push the floor away to straight arms.
breathing: In on the way down, out as you push.
safety: Elevate your hands on a bench to make it easier.

name: Machine chest press
setup: Seat height so the handles are at mid-chest.
execution: Press forward to almost straight arms.
Return slowly until you feel a chest stretch.
mistakes: Shoulders rolling forward off the pad.
safety: Easy to push close to failure safely.

name: Dip
setup: Support yourself on straight arms, shoulders down away from your ears.
execution: Lean slightly forward and lower until your upper arms are parallel to the floor.
Press back up to straight arms.
breathing: In on the way down, out as you press.
safety: Stop above any depth that pinches the front of your shoulder.

name: Cable fly
setup: Pulleys at shoulder height, one step forward, soft bend in the elbows.
execution: Hug a big tree: bring your hands together in front of your chest.
Open slowly until you feel a stretch.
breathing: Out as your hands come together.
mistakes: Turning it into a press by bending the elbows more.
safety: Keep the stretch comfortable, not forced.

name: Pec deck fly
setup: Seat so the handles are at chest height, back flat on the pad.
execution: Bring the handles together in a wide arc.
Return slowly to a comfortable stretch.
mistakes: Letting the weight pull the arms too far back.
safety: Set the start position so the stretch is comfortable.

name: Dumbbell fly
setup: Lie on a bench, dumbbells above your chest, palms facing each other.
execution: Open your arms in a wide arc with a soft elbow bend.
Squeeze them back together over your chest.
breathing: In as you open, out as you close.
mistakes: Going too heavy and too deep.
safety: Stop when your elbows reach about bench height.

name: Overhead press
setup: Bar on the front of your shoulders, grip just outside them.
Squeeze your glutes and brace your stomach.
execution: Press straight up, moving your head back out of the way.
Finish with the bar over your mid-foot, head through.
breathing: Brace before each rep; exhale near lockout.
mistakes: Leaning back into a standing incline press.
Pressing the bar out in front.
safety: If you have to lean back to finish a rep, the weight is too heavy.

name: Dumbbell shoulder press
setup: Seated with back support, dumbbells at shoulder height.
execution: Press up until your arms are straight.
Lower to just below your chin.
mistakes: Arching the back off the bench.
Clanking the dumbbells at the top.
safety: A neutral grip (palms facing in) is gentler on the shoulders.

name: Machine shoulder press
setup: Seat height so the handles start at shoulder level.
execution: Press up to almost straight arms.
Lower slowly.
mistakes: Lifting the hips off the seat.
safety: Stable and simple to push hard safely.

name: Pike push-up
setup: Start in a push-up, walk your feet in so your hips are high, like an upside-down V.
execution: Bend your elbows and lower the top of your head toward the floor in front of your hands.
Press back up.
breathing: In on the way down, out as you press.
mistakes: Hips dropping, so it turns into a push-up.
safety: Raise your feet on a box to make it harder.

name: Dumbbell lateral raise
setup: Stand tall, light dumbbells at your sides, slight bend in the elbows.
execution: Raise your arms out to the sides to shoulder height.
Lower slowly over two seconds.
safety: Light weight and strict form work best here.

name: Cable lateral raise
setup: Low pulley, handle in the far hand, cable crossing in front of your body.
execution: Raise your arm out to the side to shoulder height.
Lower under control.
mistakes: Leaning away to cheat the weight up.
safety: Keeps tension at the bottom, where dumbbells don't.

name: Face pull
setup: Rope at upper-chest height, thumbs pointing back toward you.
execution: Pull the rope toward your face, splitting the ends apart.
Finish with your hands beside your ears, then return slowly.
mistakes: Using too much weight and leaning back.
safety: Light and controlled; this is posture work, not a max lift.

name: Reverse pec deck
setup: Face the pad, handles at shoulder height.
execution: Sweep your arms back in a wide arc.
Return slowly.
mistakes: Squeezing the shoulder blades instead of moving the arms.
safety: Keep the weight light enough to control.

name: Dumbbell rear delt fly
setup: Hinge forward with a flat back, light dumbbells hanging below your chest.
execution: Raise your arms out to the sides, leading with the elbows.
Lower slowly.
safety: Rest your chest on an incline bench to spare the lower back.

name: Band pull-apart
setup: Hold a band at shoulder height, arms straight, hands shoulder-width.
execution: Pull the band apart until it touches your chest.
Return slowly.
safety: A gentle warm-up for any pressing day.

name: Barbell row
setup: Hinge forward to about 45 degrees, back flat, bar hanging at arm's length.
execution: Pull the bar to your lower ribs, elbows travelling back.
Lower under control without standing up.
breathing: Brace, pull, exhale at the top.
mistakes: Jerking the torso up to move the weight.
safety: If your lower back tires first, switch to a chest-supported row.

name: One-arm dumbbell row
setup: One knee and hand on a bench, back flat, dumbbell in the other hand.
execution: Pull the dumbbell toward your hip.
Lower to a full stretch.
mistakes: Rotating the torso to heave the weight.
safety: Supporting yourself on the bench keeps the lower back out of it.

name: Seated cable row
setup: Sit tall, feet on the platform, knees slightly bent.
execution: Pull the handle to your stomach, chest up.
Let your arms extend fully and your shoulder blades spread.
safety: Keep your torso still; let your arms and back do the work.

name: Chest-supported row
setup: Chest against the pad or an incline bench, arms hanging.
execution: Row the handles or dumbbells back, squeezing your shoulder blades.
Lower to a full stretch.
mistakes: Lifting the chest off the pad.
safety: Zero lower-back load: the go-to row when your back needs a break.

name: Inverted row
setup: Hang under a bar set at waist height, body straight, heels on the floor.
execution: Pull your chest to the bar.
Lower until your arms are straight.
safety: Bend your knees to make it easier.

name: Pull-up
setup: Hang from the bar with an overhand grip a bit wider than your shoulders.
execution: Pull your elbows down toward your ribs until your chin clears the bar.
Lower all the way to a full hang.
mistakes: Half reps from a bent-arm start.
safety: Use bands or the assisted machine until you can do 5 clean reps.

name: Chin-up
setup: Hang with palms facing you, hands shoulder-width.
execution: Pull your chest toward the bar.
Lower to a full hang.
mistakes: Craning the neck to get the chin over.
safety: Usually a little easier than pull-ups.

name: Lat pulldown
setup: Thighs locked under the pad, grip a bit wider than shoulders.
execution: Pull the bar to your upper chest, elbows driving down.
Let it rise until your arms are straight.
mistakes: Pulling the bar behind the neck.
safety: Always pull to the front of your body.

name: Assisted pull-up
setup: Knees on the assist pad, or one foot in a band looped over the bar.
execution: Pull up until your chin clears the bar.
Lower all the way.
mistakes: Using so much assistance the reps are too easy.
safety: Reduce assistance gradually as you get stronger.

name: Straight-arm pulldown
setup: High pulley, straight bar or rope, hinge forward slightly.
execution: Keeping arms almost straight, sweep the bar down to your thighs.
Let it rise slowly overhead.
mistakes: Bending the elbows into a pushdown.
safety: Light to moderate weight, full range.

name: Barbell curl
setup: Stand tall, bar at arm's length, underhand grip.
execution: Curl the bar up, elbows pinned to your sides.
Lower all the way down slowly.
safety: An EZ bar is easier on the wrists.

name: Dumbbell curl
setup: Dumbbells at your sides, palms forward.
execution: Curl up without moving your elbows.
Lower slowly to a full stretch.
mistakes: Cutting the bottom of the rep short.
safety: Simple and safe; control the lowering.

name: Hammer curl
setup: Dumbbells at your sides, palms facing in.
execution: Curl up keeping your palms facing each other.
Lower slowly.
mistakes: Swinging the dumbbells across the body.
safety: Often comfortable when regular curls bother the wrists.

name: Cable curl
setup: Low pulley with a straight bar, or a band under your feet.
execution: Curl up, elbows still.
Lower slowly.
safety: Constant tension makes lighter loads feel hard.

name: Triceps pushdown
setup: High pulley, rope or bar, elbows tucked to your sides.
execution: Push down until your arms are straight.
Let the handle rise to about chest height.
mistakes: Elbows flaring out and the shoulders helping.
safety: Keep the upper arms still.

name: Overhead triceps extension
setup: Hold one dumbbell overhead with both hands, elbows pointing forward.
execution: Lower the weight behind your head.
Extend back to straight arms.
safety: Trains the long head of the triceps in a stretch.

name: Skull crusher
setup: Lie on a bench, bar held above your chest with straight arms.
execution: Bend the elbows to lower the bar toward your forehead.
Extend back up.
safety: Lower to just behind your head rather than to your face.

name: Close-grip bench press
setup: Grip at shoulder-width, elbows tucked.
execution: Lower to your lower chest.
Press up, keeping elbows close.
breathing: Brace before lowering; exhale near the top.
mistakes: Grip so narrow the wrists bend.
safety: Use safety arms just like the regular bench press.

name: Close-grip push-up
setup: Push-up position with hands close together under your chest.
execution: Lower with elbows close to your sides.
Push back to straight arms.
breathing: In on the way down, out as you push.
safety: Do them from your knees to make them easier.

name: Plank
setup: Forearms on the floor, elbows under shoulders, body in a straight line.
execution: Squeeze your glutes and pull your ribs down.
Hold without letting your hips sag.
breathing: Slow, steady breaths through the hold.
safety: A shorter perfect hold beats a long sloppy one.

name: Side plank
setup: Lie on your side, elbow under your shoulder, feet stacked.
execution: Lift your hips so your body is straight.
Hold, then switch sides.
safety: Bend the bottom knee to make it easier.

name: Dead bug
setup: Lie on your back, arms up, hips and knees bent to 90 degrees.
execution: Lower the opposite arm and leg toward the floor, lower back pressed down.
Return and switch sides.
mistakes: Lower back arching off the floor.
safety: Very back-friendly; the core option when other areas need rest.

name: Hanging leg raise
setup: Hang from a bar, shoulders engaged.
execution: Raise your knees or straight legs by curling your pelvis up.
Lower slowly without swinging.
safety: Start with bent knees.

name: Cable crunch
setup: Kneel facing a high pulley, rope held beside your head.
execution: Crunch your ribs toward your hips, rounding your spine.
Return slowly.
mistakes: Pulling with the arms or hinging at the hips.
safety: Move from the spine, not the hips.

name: Ab wheel rollout
setup: Kneel holding the wheel under your shoulders.
execution: Roll forward as far as you can without your lower back sagging.
Pull back with your abs.
breathing: In as you roll out, out as you return.
mistakes: Lower back sagging at the far point.
safety: Roll toward a wall to limit the range at first.

name: Pallof press
setup: Stand side-on to a cable at chest height, handle at your chest.
execution: Press the handle straight out and resist the pull to rotate.
Hold, then bring it back.
safety: Trains your core to resist rotation, which protects your back.

name: Farmer's carry
setup: Pick up heavy weights in each hand like a deadlift.
execution: Walk with short, quick steps, standing tall.
Set the weights down with a flat back.
safety: Clear the path before you start.

name: Shrug
setup: Stand tall, weights at your sides.
execution: Lift your shoulders straight up toward your ears.
Pause, then lower slowly.
safety: Straight up and down only.

name: Single-leg calf raise
setup: Stand on one foot on the edge of a step, holding a rail or wall for balance.
execution: Rise onto the ball of your foot as high as you can.
Lower slowly until your heel is below the step.
safety: Hold a dumbbell in the free hand to make it harder.

name: Leg press calf raise
setup: Sit in the leg press with only the balls of your feet on the bottom edge of the platform.
Keep the safety stops engaged.
execution: Push the platform away by pointing your toes.
Return slowly into a deep stretch.
mistakes: Bending the knees to move the weight.
safety: Never take the safety stops off for this one: your feet can slip.

name: Band lateral raise
setup: Stand on the middle of a band, one end in each hand.
execution: Raise your arms out to the sides to shoulder height.
Lower slowly against the band.
safety: Easy to travel with; a lighter band is usually enough.

name: Y-raise
setup: Lie chest-down on an incline bench, or stand, holding light dumbbells, thumbs up.
execution: Raise your arms up and out into a Y shape.
Lower slowly.
mistakes: Going too heavy, so the back arches.
safety: Very light dumbbells are plenty.

name: Prone rear delt raise
setup: Lie face down on a bench or the floor, arms hanging or stretched out.
execution: Lift your arms out to the sides, squeezing your shoulder blades.
Lower slowly.
mistakes: Lifting the chest instead of the arms.
safety: Chest support keeps the lower back completely out of it.

name: Cable shrug
setup: Low pulley with a straight bar, stand tall holding it at arm's length.
execution: Lift your shoulders straight up.
Pause and lower slowly.
safety: Straight up and down only.

name: Feet-elevated push-up
setup: Push-up position with your feet on a bench or step.
execution: Lower until your chest nearly touches the floor.
Push back up, body in a straight line.
breathing: In on the way down, out as you push.
safety: The higher the feet, the more it works the shoulders.

name: Crunch
setup: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat. Fingertips lightly behind your ears.
execution: Curl your shoulders off the floor by shortening the space between ribs and hips.
Pause, then lower slowly.
breathing: Breathe out as you curl up.
mistakes: Pulling on your head with your hands.
safety: Keep your chin a fist away from your chest to spare your neck.

name: Reverse crunch
setup: Lie on your back, hips and knees bent to 90 degrees, arms by your sides.
execution: Curl your hips off the floor, bringing knees toward your chest.
Lower your hips slowly until your lower back is flat again.
breathing: Breathe out as your hips lift.
mistakes: Swinging the legs instead of curling the hips.
safety: Small, controlled lifts are enough; no need to roll onto your neck.

name: Bicycle crunch
setup: Lie on your back, hands lightly behind your head, knees lifted.
execution: Turn one shoulder toward the opposite knee as the other leg straightens.
Switch sides in a slow pedalling rhythm.
breathing: Breathe out each time you turn.
mistakes: Moving only the elbows, not the shoulders.
safety: Slow reps work the obliques far better than fast ones.

name: Lying leg raise
setup: Lie on your back, legs straight, hands under your hips or by your sides.
execution: Keeping your lower back pressed down, raise your legs to vertical.
Lower them slowly, stopping before your back arches.
breathing: Breathe out as your legs rise.
mistakes: Lower back lifting off the floor.
safety: Bend your knees to make it easier if your back starts to arch.

name: Hollow hold
setup: Lie on your back, arms overhead, legs straight.
execution: Press your lower back into the floor and lift shoulders and legs a few inches.
Hold the shallow banana shape.
mistakes: Lower back lifting away from the floor.
safety: Tuck your knees or bring your arms forward to make it easier.

name: Bird dog
setup: On hands and knees, hands under shoulders, knees under hips, back flat.
execution: Reach one arm forward and the opposite leg back until both are level with your body.
Pause, return, and switch sides.
mistakes: Hips rotating or the lower back sagging.
safety: One of the most back-friendly core exercises; good on sore days.

name: Mountain climber
setup: Start in a high plank, hands under shoulders.
execution: Drive one knee toward your chest, then switch legs.
Keep your hips level as the pace picks up.
breathing: Breathe rhythmically; don't hold your breath.
mistakes: Hands drifting forward of the shoulders.
safety: Go slower, stepping instead of jumping, if your wrists or shoulders complain.

name: Superman
setup: Lie face down, arms stretched ahead, legs straight.
execution: Lift your arms, chest and legs a few inches off the floor.
Hold for a breath, then lower with control.
mistakes: Cranking the neck back to look up.
Lifting too high and pinching the lower back.
safety: A small lift is plenty; it should feel like effort, never pain.

name: Flutter kicks
setup: Lie on your back, hands under your hips, legs straight and slightly raised.
execution: Kick your legs up and down in small, quick alternating movements.
Keep your lower back pressed down.
mistakes: Lower back arching off the floor.
safety: Raise your legs higher to make it easier on your lower back.

name: Russian twist
setup: Sit with knees bent, heels on the floor, leaning back slightly with a straight back.
execution: Rotate your chest to one side, then the other, hands moving together.
Turn from the ribs, not just the arms.
safety: Keep your feet on the floor until the movement feels smooth.

name: Single-leg glute bridge
setup: Lie on your back, one knee bent with the foot flat, the other leg straight.
execution: Drive through the planted heel to lift your hips until your body is straight from shoulder to knee.
Lower slowly. Finish all reps, then switch legs.
mistakes: Arching the lower back at the top.
safety: Squeeze the glute at the top instead of pushing higher with your back.

name: Wall sit
setup: Back flat against a wall, slide down until your thighs are about level with the floor.
execution: Hold with knees over your ankles and weight in your heels.
breathing: Slow, steady breaths through the hold.
safety: Sit higher on the wall if your knees feel any pain.

name: Jump squat
setup: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
execution: Squat down, then jump up explosively.
Land softly with bent knees and go straight into the next rep.
safety: Skip it on sore knees; bodyweight squats work the same muscles without the impact.

name: Incline push-up
setup: Hands on a sturdy raised surface (a bench, step or table edge), body in a straight line.
execution: Lower your chest to the edge.
Push back up to straight arms.
breathing: In on the way down, out as you push.
mistakes: Elbows flaring straight out to the sides.
safety: The higher your hands, the easier it gets: a great way to build up to floor push-ups.

name: Prone T raise
setup: Lie face down on a mat, arms out to the sides like a T, thumbs up.
execution: Squeeze your shoulder blades together and lift your arms a few inches.
Pause, then lower slowly.
mistakes: Lifting the chest high instead of the arms.
safety: Light and slow: these small muscles tire quickly.
